title: Incident Bot v2: least-privilege permissioning + service scopes (deploy/config/telemetry) w/ audit + break-glass
creator: Miles Thornton
description:
Goal
Implement a least-privilege permission model for Incident Bot v2 so it can fetch deploy metadata, redacted config diffs, and safe telemetry aggregations without granting broad access. All privileged access must emit audit events and support an explicit break-glass procedure for Sev0/Sev1 incidents.

Why
Bot v2 will query deploy/config/telemetry sources automatically in #incidents/#eng-oncall. Without strict scopes + auditing, we risk:
- Over-privileged service tokens (tenant data exposure)
- Unreviewed access patterns (compliance gaps)
- Confusing/unsafe escalation paths during active incidents

In scope
1) Service identity + scopes
- Create a dedicated service identity for incident-bot in production and staging.
- Define granular scopes (names tentative; align with platform conventions):
  - deploy.metadata.read (service/region/rollout phase only)
  - config.diff.read_redacted (diff limited to allowlisted keys; always redacted)
  - telemetry.query.read_safe (pre-approved aggregations only; no raw high-cardinality labels; no per-user identifiers)
  - audit.emit (write-only to audit stream)
- Ensure each backend endpoint checks BOTH:
  - caller identity (mTLS/service token)
  - requested scope(s)
- Ensure tenant scoping is enforced on the server side (bot cannot request “all tenants”; must specify incident context inputs like service/region/time window; tenant_id optional and guarded).

2) Audit events
Emit auditable events whenever the bot accesses privileged resources (including denials).
Required fields (minimum): event_name, actor_service, actor_env, request_id, incident_id (if present), slack_channel_id (if present), user_initiator (if a human action triggered it), resource_type, resource_id (or stable hash), tenant_id (if applicable), region, outcome (allow/deny), policy_version.
Event names (draft):
- incident_bot.deploy_metadata.read
- incident_bot.config_diff.read_redacted
- incident_bot.telemetry.query.read_safe
- incident_bot.break_glass.grant
- incident_bot.break_glass.revoke
- incident_bot.access.denied

3) Break-glass procedure (Sev0/Sev1)
We need a controlled escalation path for cases where:
- redacted diff is insufficient and on-call needs a wider config view
- safe telemetry aggregations are insufficient and require an expanded query template set
Constraints: must remain tenant-safe by default; any expansion must be explicit, time-bound, and audited.
Proposal:
- Break-glass is NOT automatic.
- Triggered via explicit Slack action (e.g., “Request elevated diagnostics”) visible only to on-call + SRE group.
- Requires selecting severity (Sev0/Sev1 only) + reason.
- Grants a short-lived elevation (TTL 60 minutes) for a narrow set of additional templates/fields; no secrets.
- Writes break_glass.grant and break_glass.revoke events; revoke on TTL expiry and on manual “Revoke now”.
- Document a manual fallback path if Slack is degraded (CLI/internal tool) that produces the same audit trail.

Non-goals
- Building a general-purpose RBAC UI in Console.
- Allowing raw config secret retrieval via the bot (never allowed).
- Replacing existing human-access processes for production debugging outside incidents.

Design/implementation notes
- Prefer service-to-service auth via existing platform identity (workload identity) + mTLS.
- Scopes should map to backend policy checks (policy engine) rather than being enforced only in the bot.
- For telemetry, enforce a strict server-side allowlist of query templates (e.g., GPU utilization, queue depth, KV cache pressure) with bounded time windows and aggregation rules.
- For config diffs, enforce that the endpoint only returns redacted output unless break-glass is active; even then, do not allow secrets (keep existing redaction patterns + allowlists).
- Denied requests must return a bot-friendly error message (“Missing scope: telemetry.query.read_safe”) and include a deep link to request access/break-glass when appropriate.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] incident-bot prod/staging identities created; tokens/credentials stored per standards.
- [ ] Backend endpoints for deploy/config/telemetry validate scopes; unit tests cover allow/deny.
- [ ] Audit events emitted for every privileged call (allow + deny), visible in audit log pipeline (SIEM ingestion verified).
- [ ] Break-glass flow implemented (Slack action + server gate), TTL enforced, and audited.
- [ ] Runbook snippet added: “When bot cards are empty due to permissions” + “How to break-glass in Sev0/Sev1”.
- [ ] Security sign-off from Marcus Lin / Naomi Feldman (or delegate) recorded in ticket.

Rollout plan
- Stage in staging env with synthetic incidents.
- Enable for SRE beta cohort first (feature flagged in bot v2).
- Monitor for: access.denied rate, audit event volume, break-glass usage frequency, and any unexpected tenant_id patterns.

Risks
- Overly strict scopes causing missing context in first 5 minutes (mitigate with clear bot messaging + break-glass).
- Audit event volume spikes during incidents (mitigate with sampling for non-critical denials; do not sample break-glass grants).
- Confusion between “redacted diff” vs “elevated diff” (mitigate with explicit labeling in Slack UI).

References
- ADR: incident-bot data sources + permissions (Confluence)
- Audit logging requirements: incident-bot access audit (Security/Compliance)
- Related tickets: ENG-5422 (config diff + redaction), ENG-5427 (telemetry query cache)

comments: 2025-02-19 (Miles Thornton): P0 because we saw INT-3312 (bot missing scope) and it turned into manual copy/paste debugging during Sev1. We need a stable model before GA.

2025-02-21 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Drafted scope names + mapping to policy engine checks. Will align naming with platform conventions (policy.*). Need Ethan/Mina to confirm whether deploy metadata endpoint already has service identity checks.

2025-02-24 (Kevin Osei): For audit events, please include request_id + incident_id when available. SIEM parser expects `actor_service`, `outcome`, and `resource_type`. Also confirm retention: 1 year minimum for privileged access events.
2025-02-25 (Rafael Mendes): Break-glass must work when Slack is partially degraded. Add a documented CLI/internal endpoint fallback (even if SRE-only).

2025-02-27 (Devon Price): Slack action constraints: we can gate button visibility via usergroup membership, but server-side must re-check. Also note Slack modal submit has tight ACK deadlines; keep the break-glass grant call fast (no long telemetry fanout).
2025-03-01 (Marcus Lin): Security note: elevated mode must still never return secrets. Redaction patterns should run in both modes. Also prefer TTL <= 60m and require reason string for grant.

2025-03-04 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Implemented scope checks for config diff endpoint in staging; denies correctly when bot token lacks config.diff.read_redacted. Next: wire break-glass TTL state + audit events end-to-end.

2025-03-06 (Aisha Bello): Please ensure telemetry “safe queries” includes the specific saturation templates needed for triage (GPU util, queue depth, KV cache pressure, scheduler backpressure) or we’ll end up break-glassing too often.
